rationale: Oral ground C.verum favored movement measures after MPTP and timed pole turning/descent in aged A53T mice, giving a minimal favorable motor-proxy lean against the worsening hypothesis. Small same-program studies, proxy ambiguity, an image correction and no clinical gait-speed comparison limit confidence. Human Parkinson walking benefit remains unverified.

Whole walnut oil improved evoked pain thresholds in mice, with a limited composition bridge to cold-pressed oil. Pain increased during an uncontrolled advanced-cancer diet offering a mixed-oil shake, without an oil-specific comparison. Related preparations and planned trials leave isolated Parkinson pain benefit unverified. Small nonhuman evidence, material differences and a comparator discrepancy limit the favorable lean.
